Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and the compliance items we flagged:

- HealthLynx priority: production PHI handling (EHR ingestion + clinical summarization).
- Main gating questions: BAA requirement, SOC 2 report for 2025, and whether the inference layer must be in a customer-controlled VPC or if a dedicated/reserved pool is acceptable.
- Timeline: pilot (Q3) → security review (2 weeks) → pilot onboarding (Q4).

Two asks to move fast:
1) Can you confirm whether HealthLynx will require a signed BAA before any pilot data is processed?
2) Can you share the specific SOC 2 evidence items your security team needs (e.g., full audit report, bridge letter, or specific control mappings)?

I attached the one-page demo notes and included next-step options below:

Option A — Redwood Hosted API (fastest): supports SOC2 and BAA, but tenancy is multi-tenant; we can offer encryption-at-rest, token scoping, and strict data retention controls.
Option B — Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): isolated capacity with predictable throughput; many customers choose this when they want stronger separation without on-prem.
Option C — Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed network and KMS. Required when customers insist on customer-managed infrastructure or air-gap.

I copied Karthik (infra/compliance) and Marissa (AM) to weigh in on what's typically acceptable and the evidence we can provide out of the gate.

Next steps I propose:
- Olivia: confirm BAA requirement and SOC2 scope by end of week.
- Redwood: Karthik to send an evidence bundle and sample BAA template.
- Book a 30-minute security scoping call with your CSO — available times on Friday morning PT.

Thanks, Avery — great demo. Short answers from our side:

- BAA: yes, HealthLynx requires a signed BAA before any PHI is processed in a pilot.
- SOC 2: our security team needs the Type II audit report for the most recent 12-month period and a control mapping to HIPAA where available. A bridge letter covering any gaps is helpful.
- Deployment preference: default preference is Private VPC for production. For pilot, we are open to Dedicated if we get explicit contractual controls and an isolated tenancy guarantee. Hosted API is a last resort and would require strong contractual protections and limits on data retention (we'd prefer not to use it for PHI).

Can you confirm: does Redwood provide a downloadable SOC2 report (PDF) and a BAA template we can review? Also, what is the minimum commitment for Dedicated (monthly/annual)?

CCing our CSO to coordinate a short security triage call.

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clarity. Quick technical/evidence reply and what we can provide immediately:

Evidence we can share now:
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II report (2025) — PDF (redacted where necessary).
- Standard BAA template (editable DOCX).
- Data flow diagrams for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private VPC deployment modes.

Deployment differences (short):
- Hosted API: Fast onboarding, no infra commit. We can sign a BAA, share SOC2, apply data retention policies, and enable encryption. However, compute is shared across tenants (logical isolation). Many PHI customers prefer not to put production PHI here.
- Dedicated: Isolated GPU pools reserved for your account, predictable throughput, and dedicated network endpoints. No VM-level access, but strong tenancy separation and lower blast radius. Minimum commitment: monthly reserved capacity with typical pilots starting at 1-3 months; for production we recommend quarterly or annual commitments for pricing predictability.
- Private VPC / on-prem: Customer-managed networking and KMS; we hand off the inference nodes into your VPC or on-prem package. This is the path for customers who must meet strict regulatory or audit rules requiring customer-managed infrastructure.

Attachments: I uploaded the SOC2 stub and BAA template for your security review (see attached). For the pilot, we recommend starting on Dedicated so you can iterate quickly while preserving separation; reserve Private VPC for production cutover if your audit requires it.

If helpful, I can map the specific SOC2 sections to HIPAA controls in a short doc for your CSO. When is your CSO available for a 30-minute call? Friday 11:00–12:00 PT works for Karthik and Marissa.
